items.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
items.summary: Drupal has warned of a new "highly critical" security flaw impacting Drupal core that it said has been exploited in the wild. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-136716 (CVSS score: N/A), has been described as a case of improper checking for unusual or exceptional conditions. It also relates to CVE-2026-132165 aka Fail2Install in that it addresses remaining vulnerable installation states

items.title: Proxmox 9.3 adds production snapshots for SAN-backed VMs
items.summary: Proxmox Virtual Environment 9.3 adds production support for snapshots on shared LVM storage over iSCSI and Fibre Channel SANs. items.title: U.S. CISA adds HPE, Danfoss, Mitel MiCollab, and Vates Xen Orchestra flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
items.summary: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds HPE, Danfoss, Mitel MiCollab, and Vates Xen Orchestra flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added the following HPE, Danfoss, Mitel MiCollab, and Vates Xen Orchestra flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog . CVE-2023-25914 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Path Traversal Vulnerability CVE-2023-25915 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Input Validation Vulnerability CVE-2025-41450 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Authentication Vulnerability CVE-2026-103406 Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router OS Command Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-133275 Mitel MiCollab Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability CVE-2026-133303 Mitel MiCollab XML Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-133311 Mitel MiCollab Weak Authentication Vulnerability CVE-2026-133323 Mitel MiCollab OS Command Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-133324 Mitel MiCollab Not Failing Securely Vulnerability CVE-2026-133469 Vates Xen Orchestra Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input Vulnerability The first flaw, tracked as CVE-2023-25914 (CVSS score of 7.5), is a path traversal vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration management systems running software versions prior to 3.3. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit improper restrictions on file paths to retrieve and read files from the underlying system through the XML interface. Access to sensitive files could provide information useful for further compromising the device. There are no publicly confirmed reports of exploitation in the wild or threat actors associated with this vulnerability. Danfoss addressed the issue in software version 3.3. The second flaw, tracked as CVE-2023-25915 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical improper input validation vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 800A systems running software versions prior to 3.3. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient input validation to execute arbitrary commands on the target system, potentially gaining full control of the affected refrigeration controller. Despite its critical severity and the potential consequences for operational technology environments, there are no publicly confirmed reports linking this specific vulnerability to attacks in the wild or identifying threat actors exploiting it. Danfoss released software version 3.3 to address the issue. The third flaw, tracked as CVE-2025-41450 (CVSS score of 8.2), is an improper authentication vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series systems running software versions prior to 4.2. The authentication bypass allows an attacker to generate web reports without proper authorization, potentially exposing sensitive information such as internal IP addresses, usernames and store names. The vulnerability was identified by researchers at Claroty’s Team82. Although it affects the same family of refrigeration controllers targeted in the European supermarket attacks, there is no public confirmation that attackers exploited this particular CVE during those incidents. Danfoss addressed the vulnerability in software version 4.2. The fourth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-103406 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical OS command injection vulnerability affecting HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor. The flaw resides in the AutomatedProvisioner component and allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges by supplying a specially crafted Salt minion ID. The vulnerability has been added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, confirming exploitation in the wild. However, no specific threat actor or ransomware campaign has been publicly attributed to these attacks. Administrators should apply the security updates provided by Juniper, including versions 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3 for the affected release branches. The fifth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133275 (CVSS score of 5.3), is an unrestricted file upload vulnerability affecting the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab. The vulnerability affects MiCollab version 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient file type validation to upload arbitrary files to the target system. Depending on the nature of the uploaded files and the system configuration, this could provide an opportunity for further malicious activity. Mitel has not reported confirmed exploitation in the wild or identified any threat actors associated with this vulnerability. The company released a security patch for affected installations. The sixth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133303 (CVSS score of 9.0), is a critical XML injection vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient parameter validation and leverage malicious content staged in advance to perform XML injection and execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. Successful exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the affected installation. Mitel has not disclosed any confirmed exploitation in the wild or identified threat actors behind attacks exploiting this flaw. A security patch is available for affected MiCollab installations. The seventh flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133311 (CVSS score of 5.9), is an improper authentication vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker who knows a specific system-generated random identifier or has access to malicious content staged in advance could exploit the weakness to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. No confirmed exploitation or associated threat actors have been publicly reported. Mitel has released a security patch to address the issue. The eighth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS score of 10.0), is a critical OS command injection vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient parameter sanitization to perform blind command injection and execute arbitrary commands within the context of the affected system. Successful exploitation could compromise system integrity and availability. Mitel has not reported confirmed exploitation in the wild or attributed attacks to specific threat actors. A security patch is available to address the vulnerability. The ninth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133324 (CVSS score of 5.3), is an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. Improper handling of authentication could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass security controls and perform unauthorized actions within the application. Successful exploitation could compromise the security of the affected installation. No publicly confirmed exploitation or associated threat actors have been reported. Mitel has released a security patch for the affected versions. The tenth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133469 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability affecting Vates Xen Orchestra, a management and backup platform for XCP-ng and XenServer environments. The vulnerability affects versions prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit improper handling of authentication tokens by supplying a specially crafted cookie containing an empty JSON object. The application may then authenticate the attacker as the owner of an existing, unexpired token. Once authenticated, the attacker could retrieve reusable authentication token identifiers, potentially enabling persistent unauthorized access to the environment. The vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild , although no specific threat actors have been publicly identified. Vates addressed the issue in Xen Orchestra versions 6.9.2 and 6.10.1. The Danfoss vulnerabilities deserve particular attention because they affect the same family of refrigeration management systems involved in the cyberattacks targeting European supermarkets in October and November 2026. The first wave of attacks, detected between October 11 and 12, compromised refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail sites in France. Attackers manipulated defrost settings, forcing refrigeration equipment to operate at excessively high temperatures. The incidents resulted in substantial food losses and at least 15 reported fires. A second wave between November 1 and 2 affected retailers across several other European countries. The French authorities’ investigation attributed the October attacks to Shahid Kaveh , a cyber unit associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). However, responsibility for the subsequent November attacks across Europe has not been conclusively established. The technical evidence points to the exploitation of internet-exposed refrigeration management interfaces, with default credentials and outdated firmware considered likely entry points. However, investigators have not confirmed that CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915 or CVE-2025-41450 were specifically exploited during these operations. The incidents instead highlight the risks associated with exposing operational technology (OT) systems directly to the internet without adequate authentication, network segmentation and security updates. An additional development is worth mentioning: a November 2026 advisory from Ireland’s National Cyber Security Centre reported research by Midnight Blue identifying six previously unknown pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM 800A controllers, affecting firmware versions up to and including 5.3.2. At the time of the advisory, these flaws had not yet received CVE identifiers and no patches were available. Researchers also warned that attackers could establish persistence surviving factory resets and firmware updates. These findings add another layer of concern to the security of refrigeration infrastructure. ncsc.gov.ie According to Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities , FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog. Experts also recommend that private organizations review the Catalog and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure. CISA order U.S. federal civilian agencies to remediate eight of them by November 28, 2026, and the remaining two by December 9, 2026. The individual deadlines are: November 28, 2026: CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2026-103406, CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133323, CVE-2026-133324 and CVE-2026-133469. December 9, 2026: CVE-2025-41450 and CVE-2026-133311. Follow me on Twitter: @securityaffairs and Facebook and Mastodon Pierluigi Paganini ( SecurityAffairs – hacking, CISA )

  • CVE-2023-25914 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Path Traversal Vulnerability
  • CVE-2023-25915 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Input Validation Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2025-41450 Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Improper Authentication Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-103406 Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133275 Mitel MiCollab Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133303 Mitel MiCollab XML Injection Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133311 Mitel MiCollab Weak Authentication Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133323 Mitel MiCollab OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133324 Mitel MiCollab Not Failing Securely Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-133469 Vates Xen Orchestra Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input Vulnerability 

The first flaw, tracked as CVE-2023-25914 (CVSS score of 7.5), is a path traversal vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration management systems running software versions prior to 3.3. An authenticated remote attacker could exploit improper restrictions on file paths to retrieve and read files from the underlying system through the XML interface. The second flaw, tracked as CVE-2023-25915 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical improper input validation vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 800A systems running software versions prior to 3.3. The third flaw, tracked as CVE-2025-41450 (CVSS score of 8.2), is an improper authentication vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series systems running software versions prior to 4.2. The fourth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-103406 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical OS command injection vulnerability affecting HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor. The flaw resides in the AutomatedProvisioner component and allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges by supplying a specially crafted Salt minion ID. The fifth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133275 (CVSS score of 5.3), is an unrestricted file upload vulnerability affecting the Audio, Web and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab. The vulnerability affects MiCollab version 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier. Depending on the nature of the uploaded files and the system configuration, this could provide an opportunity for further malicious activity. The sixth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133303 (CVSS score of 9.0), is a critical XML injection vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient parameter validation and leverage malicious content staged in advance to perform XML injection and execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. Successful exploitation could compromise the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the affected installation. Mitel has not disclosed any confirmed exploitation in the wild or identified threat actors behind attacks exploiting this flaw. A security patch is available for affected MiCollab installations.

The seventh flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133311 (CVSS score of 5.9), is an improper authentication vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker who knows a specific system-generated random identifier or has access to malicious content staged in advance could exploit the weakness to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. No confirmed exploitation or associated threat actors have been publicly reported. Mitel has released a security patch to address the issue.

The eighth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS score of 10.0), is a critical OS command injection vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit insufficient parameter sanitization to perform blind command injection and execute arbitrary commands within the context of the affected system. A security patch is available to address the vulnerability.

The ninth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133324 (CVSS score of 5.3), is an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting the AWV component of Mitel MiCollab. Successful exploitation could compromise the security of the affected installation. No publicly confirmed exploitation or associated threat actors have been reported. Mitel has released a security patch for the affected versions.

The tenth flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-133469 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability affecting Vates Xen Orchestra, a management and backup platform for XCP-ng and XenServer environments. The vulnerability affects versions prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1. According to Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog.

Experts also recommend that private organizations review the Catalog and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure.

CISA order U.S. federal civilian agencies to remediate eight of them by November 28, 2026, and the remaining two by December 9, 2026. The individual deadlines are:

  • November 28, 2026: CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2026-103406, CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133323, CVE-2026-133324 and CVE-2026-133469.

items.title: More than 4,400 malicious domains are waiting for holiday shoppers
items.summary: Cybercriminals are positioned to exploit the holiday shopping season through fraudulent storefronts, retailer impersonation, payment fraud and account takeover attacks, according to FortiGuard Labs’ Holiday Season Cyber Threats Report 2026. Researchers identified more than 24,000 newly registered domains containing keywords associated with seasonal shopping over a 90-day period, including more than 4,400 classified as malicious. Underground marketplaces are facilitating the trade in stolen customer information, access to e-commerce infrastructure and services that support financial fraud. … More →

items.title: Google mandates MCP or CLI access for Workspace AI agents starting February 2027
items.summary: Google has announced security controls across Google Workspace and Google Cloud to address the risks associated with autonomous AI agents accessing enterprise data, executing tasks, and interacting with cloud infrastructure. The measures include dedicated agent identities, human approval controls for sensitive operations, prompt injection screening, and restrictions on how third-party AI tools access and process organizational data. The company also announced the general availability of its Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and command-line interface … More →
